text:
CHIEF: I AM REVERSING MY OWN PRIORITY. NFRD GOES BACK TO PRIMARY; gptkz BECOMES CONTINGENT ON TWO
OWNER DECISIONS. root's inspection settled it in twenty minutes and both of my reasons for
promoting gptkz turned out to be wrong.

WHAT root ESTABLISHED, by looking rather than reasoning:

  The paper's Appendix 1 prints the full 328-WORD BARTLETT STIMULUS. Recoverable even though the
  OSF deposit is not anonymously accessible. Good.

  OUR TEXT IS NOT THAT TEXT. root compared them directly: our Boas/Cultee source is 425 tokens
  and CONTAINS EVENTS AND CLAUSES ABSENT FROM THE EXPERIMENT. So the checksum, the spans, and
  some situations cannot be reused. A distinct source version and a newly evidenced story
  artifact are required.

  gptkz RETURNS 401 AND REDIRECTS TO SIGN-IN. Raw-reproduction presence, deposit licence and
  chain-key integrity are all UNKNOWN -- which is to say the single question I told root to answer
  first, corpus-or-spreadsheet, IS STILL UNANSWERED and cannot be answered from here.

  THE STIMULUS LICENCE IS NOT CLEARED. The article is CC BY 4.0, but the stimulus is credited to
  Bartlett 1932, so the article's licence does not obviously convey redistribution rights over it.

SO BOTH LEGS OF MY ARGUMENT ARE GONE. I promoted gptkz over NFRD because "the source side is
already done" -- it is done for a DIFFERENT TEXT -- and because it looked like a fast win, when in
fact it is behind a sign-in wall and a copyright question. NFRD is CC0, openly accessible, and its
GitHub repository answered HTTP 200 on the first probe. It is now the better route on every axis
except stimulus familiarity.

NFRD IS PRIMARY AGAIN. root: resume bd-01M17FAGN83C3ZT2VZ2VKHWTYJ as the main line, with the
observation-versus-derivation field classification I required, and remember Sherlock is the
control for what NFRD's filler-and-repetition removal costs.

TWO THINGS ONLY THE OWNER CAN DECIDE, and I am not deciding either:

  1. OSF ACCESS. gptkz needs an account or token. Anonymous is 401. This is not something an
     agent should solve by creating credentials.

  2. WHETHER WE MAY USE THE BARTLETT 1932 STIMULUS AT ALL. Bartlett died in 1969, so under
     life-plus-seventy his edited stimulus is plausibly in copyright until 2039. That is very
     likely why WarOfTheGhostsText.scala uses Boas 1901 in the first place -- our own fixture
     header says Bartlett's version "is not yet in the public domain" and anticipates "a lab copy
     may be registered as a second fixture version later". Somebody already thought about this and
     chose the public-domain text deliberately.

     The question is not whether we can read it. It is whether a fixture built on it can ship in a
     library the owner intends to publish. That constrains what this library may BECOME, which is
     the owner's call and not mine.

gptkz STAYS OPEN AND WORTH DOING, on a lower priority, unblocked the moment either decision lands.
If the owner obtains OSF access and the raw reproductions are there, the modelling work is real
but no longer free: a second source version over the Bartlett wording, newly evidenced, with its
own checksum.

root: no stimulus or participant text in git, correctly. Keep it that way until the licence
question is answered rather than assumed.
